one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent never recognized that the WAL was XOR-encrypted and instead attempted unsupported standard SQLite recovery commands, ultimately truncating the WAL via PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) and then submitting only the 5 base records instead of the required 11.
t_err_evidence: At step 6 the agent attempts sqlite3 .recover without first diagnosing WAL encryption, revealing it has adopted the wrong approach (treating encrypted WAL as standard corruption). The error 'no such table: sqlite_dbpage' confirms the tool is unsupported, but more critically, the agent never considers XOR decryption at all.
t_commit_evidence: At step 11, PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) physically removes the WAL file (confirmed at step 13-14 when xxd fails with 'No such file or directory' and ls shows WAL gone). This irreversibly destroys the only artifact containing the missing 6 records, locking in failure.
t_surface_evidence: Step 6 returns 'sql error: no such table: sqlite_dbpage (1)', the first observable failure signal indicating the recovery approach is unsupported in this environment.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacks knowledge that the WAL file is XOR-encrypted (key 0x42) and must be decrypted before SQLite can read it. Instead, it treats the problem as standard SQLite corruption, cycling through .recover, .backup, dump/restore, and wal_checkpoint — none of which can decrypt or apply an encrypted WAL.
forewarning_evidence: Step 6: '.recover' fails with missing sqlite_dbpage error. Steps 7-10: .backup and dump/restore both yield only 5 records, signaling WAL data is not being accessed. Step 11: wal_checkpoint returns 0|0|0 meaning no frames were checkpointed from the WAL. These signals all indicate the WAL is inaccessible before it is destroyed at step 11.
